what_this_is: The per-check AXIS DECOMPOSITION for the OC checks C1a's crosswalk lands an edge on and A3 did NOT decompose. A3 committed 13 of the 175; its scope block hands the other 162 to C1. This file holds C1a's, C1b-i's and C1b-ii's share of them and nothing else.
why_a_second_file_and_not_an_edit_of_A3s: Editing docs/conformance/oc-axes-2026-07-28.json would give one artefact two owners — the MES-24 two-censuses defect, where the two disagree and nothing detects it. A3 owns its 13; C1 owns what C1 extracts. Disjointness is ASSERTED BY THE BUILDER (mix conformance.crosswalk refuses on any overlap), not left to a convention. PM-ratified as D4, MES-97 comment 27858.
axis_source_rule: AXES COME FROM THE PREDICATE, NEVER FROM THE DESCRIPTION — docs/conformance/match-relation.md §2, cited not restated.
difference_from_A3s_13: A3's 13 are all `a(...)`-form checks whose predicate is an inline arrow function, so every axis expression is a substring of the emitting excerpt itself. NONE of the checks here is like that: every one computes its predicate into a minified binding BEFORE the emitting call, and three of them are decided at a site that is not the emitting site at all. C1b-ii's 9 are the sharpest case — their verdict is `i.length===0` / `o.length===0` over an error accumulator filled by a ternary several hundred bytes earlier, so EVERY axis expr lives in a `context_excerpt` and none in the evaluator excerpt. So each row carries `context_excerpts` — further addressed spans the predicate depends on — and an axis `expr` is a verbatim substring of the evaluator excerpt OR of one of them. The row says which, in `expr_found_in`.

provenance.emitting_spans_from: docs/conformance/oc-emitting-sites-2026-07-28.json — generated by mix conformance.locator, not re-cut by hand
provenance.context_spans_from: located by unique-substring search against the same build; each is unique in it
provenance.bytes_are_not_stored_here: Spans only. `mix conformance.crosswalk` lifts the bytes LIVE from the build at these spans and refuses if any axis `expr` is not a verbatim substring of what it lifted. Storing the bytes here as well would create a second copy that can drift from the build without anything noticing — the same reasoning bucket-0 gives for lifting rather than remembering.

polarity_rule: `pass_when_true` — the expression being TRUE is the passing arm. `fail_when_true` — the expression being TRUE is the failing arm. Read off the branch the excerpt actually writes, never off the requirement's wording.
preconditions_rule: A list of `{guard, kind, on_failure, reads}`. A precondition is NOT an axis, and the reason is NOT the status it writes: it is that the guard reads something OTHER than a behaviour of the implementation under test — the harness's own transport, whether a diagnostic tool is listed, whether the probe was run at all — so an ET claim can neither agree with it nor contradict it, and `shape_from_axes/1` never sees one. C1a stated the rule as `its failure makes the check not evaluate (SKIPPED)`, and C1c-i measured that that is NOT what the artefacts do: A3's own server-stateless rows record `()=>n?` and `()=>S?` and `!r||!i` as preconditions whose `on_failure` is an ERROR MESSAGE, and the check goes red. Three `on_failure` shapes occur in this file and each is written as what it is — `SKIPPED` (ServerIdentifiesInResultMeta's `if(_)return{skipped:!0`, and the two `listChanged` rows' capability guards), a FAILURE naming the probe, and a WARNING carrying `details:{untestable:!0}`. The rule as C1a wrote it would have forced a dozen harness-transport guards to be recorded as AXES, and every ET claim would then have been `silent` on them — which makes every red-OC edge `:partial` and bucket 4b by construction, and would have made A3 §3's `(red, green, :full)` escalation UNREACHABLE on the first leg where it can occur. Restating the rule on its actual ground is therefore not a loosening; it is what stops the decomposition deciding an adjudication.

scope.the_figure_this_field_used_to_carry_was_: It said `The remaining 123 of the 173` and the answer at that commit was 111, not 123 — measured by regenerating the set from d5cac00's own copy of this file. The author's predicate is recoverable from the arithmetic: 173 - 49 - 1 = 123, i.e. this file's 49 rows plus the ONE A3 row the block above names by hand, forgetting A3's other TWELVE. So it was not drift and re-measuring at a later tip would not have found it; it was a subtraction over the wrong minuend from the day it was written. scope.the_eighteen_C1c_i_adds: C1c-i declares the `server-stateless` scenario — 30 in-denominator checks — so G19 forces every one of the 30 to be decomposed before any of them can be reported in bucket 2. They are CITED from A3's file and NOT re-homed here (D4, and `axis_index/1` refuses the overlap). scope.how_the_18_were_cut: The method, stated once here because C1c-ii/iii/iv inherit it. START at the locator's `emitting_byte_span` for the row — never at a grep. WIDEN to the enclosing balanced expression, which for these rows the locator has already done: 15 of the 18 are `rung: id_literal_pair` pinned at level `row` with a single site, and the three RequestMetaInvalid rows are `id_template_prefix` pinned at level `loop`, where one site emits three rows. READ the axes off the branch the excerpt WRITES: one axis per conjunct of the deciding test, `expr` verbatim, polarity from the arm that carries `error` rather than from the requirement's wording. Where the predicate reads a name bound OUTSIDE the excerpt, locate the binding by UNIQUE SUBSTRING search and record it as a `context_excerpt` with the reason it is needed — every context span in the 18 was located that way and each is unique in the build. NOTHING here stores bytes: the generator lifts them live under `--harness` and refuses any `expr`, `guard` or listed conjunct that is not a verbatim substring of what it lifted.
scope.what_the_18_cost_against_the_client_leg: Lighter per row than CG7's 29, and measured rather than assumed: CG7 needed FOUR `locator_row_rejected` rows and 24 rows carrying `check_id_found_in`, because its ids are computed from argument values. All 18 here are `locator_row` — not one rejects the locator's span — and only the three RequestMetaInvalid rows need anything beyond the default id location. The 18 yield 26 axes; CG7's 29 yielded 47.

emitting_span_provenance_rule: Every row states where its `emitting_byte_span` came from, and the generator CHECKS the statement against MES-97's locator output (G18). `locator_row` — the span is one the locator names for this row's key, and the generator requires that. `locator_row_rejected` — the locator's own `rung_pin_level` for that row is NOT `row`, so it does not claim to pin the row; the span it names belongs to a sibling and is refused. The generator then requires the reverse: the pin level must not be `row`, the span used must NOT be one of the locator's, and a reason must be given. Four of C1b-i's 29 rows are rejections; C1a's 11 are all `locator_row`, and were so before this field existed. C1b-ii's 9 are all `locator_row` TOO, and each carries an `emitting_span_provenance_why` anyway — not because G18 demands one on an acceptance (it does not), but because the locator pins these rows at level CHECK and names three sites for every one of them, so G18 would accept the Name push against a Method row and vice versa. The acceptance is honest and the residual it leaves is stated on the row rather than in this rule. C1b-iii's 4 are all `locator_row`, and ONE of them — DefaultResultTypeComplete — is the same shape again and carries its own `emitting_span_provenance_why`: the locator pins it at level CHECK and names FOUR sites, two of which are not this check's pushes at all but unrelated code binding some `i`. Saying so on the row is the whole remedy available here; G18 cannot distinguish them, and pretending otherwise would be the AC7 error.
check_id_location_rule: C1a's 11 rows all carry their check id as a backtick literal at the emitting site, and the generator required exactly that. Fourteen of C1b-i's rows emit with `id:c` — a value COMPUTED from the argument's value and declared type — and ten more with `id:t`, a loop variable. So a row may name `check_id_found_in`: the pool entry whose bytes must carry the id literal. It defaults to `evaluator_excerpt`, which is C1a's behaviour unchanged, and the named entry must exist. This WEAKENS the guard from `the id is at the emitting site` to `the id is verbatim at an ADDRESSED span this row names`, and that is said plainly rather than left to be noticed: what it still refuses is a row whose id occurs nowhere it points at. C1b-iii adds one more user of the field — DefaultResultTypeComplete, which emits with `id:i` where `i` is bound to the literal one statement earlier, so the literal is in the guard excerpt and nowhere near either push. C1c-i meets a third shape and it is the first that NO span can satisfy. The `server-stateless` RequestMetaInvalid trio emits with ``id:`sep-2575-request-meta-invalid-${e.slug}` `` and the composed ids occur NOWHERE in the build — measured, 0 hits each for `sep-2575-request-meta-invalid-missing-meta`, `-missing-protocol-version` and `-missing-client-capabilities` in the 809 KB dist — so `check_id_found_in` cannot help whichever span it names. Such a row states `check_id_composition` instead: a `template` verbatim at a named span, a `hole` occurring EXACTLY ONCE in it, and a `substitution` verbatim at another named span, with the substituted result required to equal the check id EXACTLY. The two fields are mutually exclusive — two answers to one question, and nothing would choose between them. This is NOT a further weakening: the literal form asks `is the id at a span you name`, and the composed form asks the same question of every PART of the id, with the template pinned to the build so the only freedom is the one hole. A row cannot cover the id with fragments it found lying around (the S9-18 shape), because a degenerate cover would have to be a template that is verbatim in the dist and contains the hole, which is the emitting site itself.
